resources.string: Vita3K needs Sony\'s PS Vita firmware (PSVUPDAT.PUP) and font package (PSP2UPDAT.PUP). Set up shows where to download both and installs them.
Install your own copy of the game: a .pkg with its license (work.bin or zRIF), or a .vpk or .zip dump.
PKG, VPK, ZIP or a license
Touch gestures instead of on-screen buttons
A short buzz when a hold, Select or the menu gesture registers
A short swipe pushes the stick %1$d%% of the way, so he walks; longer swipes push it further, so he runs. If short swipes still run, slide left. If he doesn\'t move, slide right.
A swipe about %1$s mm long pushes the stick all the way, so he runs. Slide left to run with shorter swipes.
For any menu that ignores the stick. The D-pad moves him at full speed in only 4 directions.
Hold one finger, swipe with another
Two-finger tap, then two-finger tap and hold
While one finger walks, a second finger can tap for Cross, hold for Circle or swipe to turn the camera. To hold Circle while walking, hold, then drag the same finger.
Circle, held for as long as your finger stays down
Select, held for as long as your fingers stay down
Left stick, any direction: a short swipe walks, a longer one runs
Right stick: turns the camera, following the swiping finger

Persona 4 Golden only draws 16:9. 4:3 crop shows the middle of the picture, bigger, and cuts off its sides along with anything drawn there. 4:3 squeeze fits the whole picture into 4:3, so everything looks narrower. Fill stretches it over the whole screen.
Skips the game\'s ghosting effect. Turn off if anything looks wrong.
No blur pass seen in the last frame.
Last frame: %1$d of %2$d full-screen read-backs removed.
A screenshot of these lines shows exactly how the game draws its blur, to fine-tune the fix.
Draws a frame on every screen refresh instead of every other one.
Draws a frame on every screen refresh instead of every other one. Now: %1$d FPS.
Looking for the game\'s time per frame (1/30 s)…
No 1/30 s values found in the game yet.
Found %1$d time-per-frame values in the game\'s data and %2$d in its code.
Also fix the values in the game\'s code
Takes effect the next time the game starts, and turning it off too.

At 60 FPS the game may run twice as fast. The speed fix changes its time per frame from 1/30 s to 1/60 s. Walk around and check the speed: try All first. If the game breaks or still runs fast, try one value at a time, then the switch for the code values.
